sentences.text:
This petition is filed by the petitioner in Crime No.112/2021 arising out of PCR No.161/2020 registered by the Kanakapura Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 506,504,
419, 420, 465, 471, 323, 324 and 468 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC').
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, learned HCGP for the State and learned counsel for the respondent No.2 3.

The case of the prosecution is that on the compliant of Shivamallaiah, the respondent No.2/defacto complainant, filed a private complaint before the Magistrate in PCR NO.161/2020 alleging that he has got some property under the compromise deed in O.S.NO.387/2008.

That he is having some ear and eye impairment and his family members have not look after him well and taking advantage of his situation, the petitioner being NC: 2024:KHC:10820 brother-in-law or son of his sister wanted to take him to the eye clinic, in the name of the surgery and then petitioner/accused said to have taken him to the Sub-Registrar office and got sale deed registered in respect of the said property.
He has not paid any single rupee, therefore, when he wanted to construct the building he obtained the revenue records and came to know that the accused already got his name in the revenue records.

Hence he has approached the court for cancelling the sale deed,
but the accused said to have assaulted on 2.11.2020.
Hence, he has approached police for lodging the complaint but they refused to receive.
Thereafter, he went to the Superintendent of Police, they also not registered the FIR.
Hence, he was forced to file complaint before the Magistrate and got it referred to the police under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.
In turn the police registered the FIR after receiving of the complaint from the Magistrate, which is under challenge.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has seriously contended the respondent already filed civil suit for cancelling the sale deed.
The case is purely civil in nature.
There is no criminality or intention to cheat the complainant.

The amount NC: 2024:KHC:10820 has been paid by the petitioner to the deceased-respondent No.2 and on the date of registration Rs.1,75,000/- has been paid and also Rs.4 lakh was paid prior to the registration on various dates.

Therefore, the criminal case is not Sri Vijayakumar Y P vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149281802/
2 sustainable.

entities.text: Sri Vijayakumar Y P vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, prayed for quashing the FIR.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent and learned HCGP objected the petition contending, that the petitioner has not at all paid any sale consideration of Rs.4,75,000/- even otherwise Rs.3,90,000/- has been withdrawn by the petitioner from the account of the respondent and the matter is required for interrogation, where the petitioner took the complainant who is uncle aged about more than 75 years.
He has misrepresented and the complainant was taken by the petitioner to the Sub-registrar Office and without making any payment, the sale deed got executed.
Therefore, matter is required for investigation.
Hence, prayed for dismissing the petition.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent also submits though the suit was filed in the year 2021 till today petitioner not filed written statement.
Having heard the arguments, perused the records.

On perusal of the same ofcourse, the respondent approached the police, as well as higher authority of the police and he has followed the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA AND ANOTHER vs.
STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND OTHERS reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287.

PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA AND ANOTHER vs.
STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND OTHERS reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, private complaint came to be filed and got it referred to the police under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. here the respondent has stated, he is absolute owner of the property measuring 0.10 guntas situated at Kanakapura village.

The petitioner being brother-in-law or son of the sister of the respondent No.2 took him to the Sub-Registrar office and got registered the sale deed without making any payment and they have sold the same for Rs.5,75,000/- as a sale consideration given by way of cash.
On perusal of this alleged sale deed there is no mention of date of payment made by the petitioner for Rs.4 lakh by cash to the deceased respondent on various dates.
It is only mentioned in the sale deed for Rs.1,75,000/- on the date of registration by cash, the remaining amount there is no date mentioned for that.

The respondent No.2 contention that he had impaired, as well as his eyes also not properly NC: 2024:KHC:10820 visible and the petitioner being the son of the sister, took him to the hospital in the name of eye clinic.
But he was taken to the Sub-registrar office and got registered the sale deed.
Ofcourse the respondent No.2 already filed suit in OS.No.618/2021 which is pending where the petitioner not yet filed written statement for last 3 years.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, the legal heirs of the respondent No.2 also filed suit for partition, which is pending in that case also and there is no written statement filed by the petitioner,
two civil suits are pending.
However, main allegation against the petitioner that the petitioner cheated the complainant and also assaulted on 2.11.2020 at 11.30 a.m., when he approached the accused for cancelling the sale deed.
Ofcourse the Hon'ble Supreme Court held, when the civil cases are pending the criminal cases cannot be taken as the matter has been seized by the civil court.
But here in this case, the complainant already filed criminal case against the petitioner.
Subsequently, he has filed civil suit for cancelling the sale deed.

The matter required for investigation, whether the petitioner took the complainant to the Sub-registrar office and paid any amount in presence of the witnesses for NC: 2024:KHC:10820 Rs.4,75,000/- which is matter of investigation.

Therefore, that cannot be looked into by the civil court at this state, even if the police investigate the matter, and file Sri Vijayakumar Y P vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149281802/
3 final report that may help the civil court for coming to the right conclusions for cancelling the sale deed.

sentences.text: Such being the case, I am of the view, it is not a fit case for quashing the FIR at this stage.
Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
